answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The juniper multiplier is published, charged in horizon, and mirror lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1349 identities would post 2196 proofs and burn roughly 39 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
